csharp/workspace:src/LibTmux.Workspace.C.content:
# tmux-workspace [![LibTmux.Workspace.Cli](https://img.shields.io/nuget/v/LibTmux.Workspace.Cli?label=LibTmux.Workspace.Cli)](https://www.nuget.org/packages/LibTmux.Workspace.Cli) [![libtmux.org](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-libtmux.org-0b7285)](https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/) [![build](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-dotnet/actions/workflows/dotnet.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-dotnet/actions/workflows/dotnet.yml) [![tmux 3.3a – 3.8](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-dotnet/actions/workflows/dotnet-tmux.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-dotnet/actions/workflows/dotnet-tmux.yml) Describe a tmux session once, in YAML, and open it with one command. [`tmux-workspace`][api-workspace-cli] reads [tmuxp](https://github.com/tmux-python/tmuxp) workspace files, captures running sessions back into them, and answers in JSON when a script asks.
> **Releases.** Releases are numbered `0.1.N`, and each release increments `N`. > The API is not settled: any release may change or remove exported identifiers, > and the changelog marks each break. Pin an exact version to avoid one. ## Quick start Install the tool, then save a workspace as `~/.tmuxp/myproject.yaml`: ```console $ dotnet tool install --global LibTmux.Workspace.Cli ``` The file describes one session: ```yaml session_name: myproject start_directory: ~/code/myproject windows: - window_name: editor layout: main-vertical panes: - vim - git status - window_name: server panes: - npm run dev ``` Open it: ```console $ tmux-workspace load myproject ``` Outside tmux this attaches your terminal to the new session. Inside tmux it asks whether to switch to it, leave it detached, or add its windows to the session you are in. ## Install The quick start installs the tool globally. If your shell cannot find `tmux-workspace` afterwards, add `$HOME/.dotnet/tools` to `PATH`. Try it without installing anything, using the .NET 10 SDK: ```console $ dnx LibTmux.Workspace.Cli --yes -- --help ``` Pin it for everyone who clones a repository. Run this at the repository root, commit the `dotnet-tools.json` it writes, and run the tool as `dotnet tmux-workspace`: ```console $ dotnet tool install LibTmux.Workspace.Cli ``` Upgrade a global install: ```console $ dotnet tool update --global LibTmux.Workspace.Cli ``` ## Commands ### [`tmux-workspace load`][api-workspace-cli-load]: build a session from a workspace file Load a workspace without attaching: ```console $ tmux-workspace load -d myproject ``` Load the `.tmuxp.yaml` in a project directory: ```console $ tmux-workspace load ~/code/myproject ``` Load a workspace on a named tmux socket. Choose a name reserved for this workspace: `-L` selects an endpoint and may join a server already using that name: ```console $ tmux-workspace load -d -L demo myproject ``` Attach to that socket with tmux: ```console $ tmux -L demo attach ``` Without `-L` or `-S`, `LIBTMUX_SOCKET_PATH` names a socket by path and `LIBTMUX_SOCKET` by name. The flags win over both, and the path wins over the name. With neither variable set the tool passes tmux no socket, and tmux picks the server: the one in `TMUX` from inside tmux, otherwise its default socket. A `load` that may switch to or append to your session asks for the `TMUX` server by name. Load several workspaces at once; the last one is the one you land in: ```console $ tmux-workspace load api web ``` Add a workspace's windows to the tmux session you are in: ```console $ tmux-workspace load --append tools ``` ### [`tmux-workspace ls`][api-workspace-cli-ls]: what it can find List the workspaces it can find: ```console $ tmux-workspace ls ``` Group the list by directory: ```console $ tmux-workspace ls --tree ``` ### [`tmux-workspace search`][api-workspace-cli-search]: find by name, window, or pane command Find the workspaces that mention `server` in their name, windows, or pane commands: ```console $ tmux-workspace search server ``` ### [`tmux-workspace freeze`][api-workspace-cli-freeze]: save a running session Save a running session as a workspace file: ```console $ tmux-workspace freeze myproject --save-to ~/.tmuxp/myproject.yaml ``` ### [`tmux-workspace convert`][api-workspace-cli-convert]: YAML to JSON and back Convert a workspace between YAML and JSON: ```console $ tmux-workspace convert myproject.yaml --save-to myproject.json ``` ### [`tmux-workspace import`][api-workspace-cli-import]: tmuxinator and teamocil projects Turn a tmuxinator project into a workspace: ```console $ tmux-workspace import tmuxinator ~/.config/tmuxinator/blog.yml \ --save-to ~/.tmuxp/blog.yaml ``` Or a teamocil one: ```console $ tmux-workspace import teamocil ~/.teamocil/blog.yml \ --save-to ~/.tmuxp/blog.yaml ``` ### [`tmux-workspace edit`][api-workspace-cli-edit]: open a workspace in `$EDITOR` Open a workspace in `$EDITOR`: ```console $ tmux-workspace edit myproject ``` ### [`tmux-workspace debug-info`][api-workspace-cli-debug-info]: details for a bug report Collect versions and search paths for a bug report: ```console $ tmux-workspace debug-info ``` ### [`tmux-workspace shell`][api-workspace-cli-shell]: a Python REPL on a session Open a Python REPL holding a session's tmux objects. It runs through tmuxp 1.74.0, so point `TMUX_WORKSPACE_PYTHON` at a Python that has it installed: ```console $ tmux-workspace shell myproject ``` `tmux-workspace --help` lists every option. ## Workspace files A command that takes a workspace accepts a file path, a directory holding a `.tmuxp.yaml`, or a bare name. A name is looked up in the first of these that exists: 1. `$TMUXP_CONFIGDIR` 2. `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tmuxp`, which defaults to `~/.config/tmuxp` 3. `~/.tmuxp` `ls` also shows the nearest `.tmuxp.yaml`, `.tmuxp.yml`, or `.tmuxp.json` above the current directory. The format is tmuxp's, in YAML or JSON. The [configuration reference](https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/configuration/) covers every key, and the [example gallery](https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/examples/gallery/) has files to start from. ## Scripting [`--json`][api-workspace-output] prints one JSON document on stdout. `--ndjson` streams one record per line as a load progresses. Errors go to stderr as JSON lines with a stable `code`. List workspace names: ```console $ tmux-workspace ls --json | jq -r '.workspaces[].name' ``` Load detached and read back which sessions were created: ```console $ tmux-workspace load -d --json myproject | jq -r '.results[].session_name' ``` Inside tmux, a scripted `load` needs `-d` or `--append`, because a script cannot answer the switch prompt. [`ls`][api-workspace-cli-ls] and [`search`][api-workspace-cli-search] print the same JSON as tmuxp. | Exit status | Meaning | |---|---| | 0 | Done | | 1 | The operation failed; `status` and the error `code` say how | | 2 | Usage: a bad option, or a command that cannot run where it was started | | 70 | An internal error; please report it | | 130 | Interrupted | The [output reference](https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/reference/output/) and [error codes](https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/reference/exit-codes/) document every field. ## Shell completion Bash, with the bash-completion package: ```console $ tmux-workspace --generate bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/tmux-workspace ``` zsh, into any directory on your `fpath`: ```console $ tmux-workspace --generate zsh > ~/.zfunc/_tmux-workspace ``` fish: ```console $ tmux-workspace --generate fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/tmux-workspace.fish ``` [`--generate man`][api-workspace-completion] writes a manual page. ## Differences from tmuxp - A window with no `layout` is tiled. tmuxp keeps halving the last pane. - Without a `focus` key the first window is left active. tmuxp leaves the last. - `-8` is refused, because no supported tmux implements 88-color mode. Use `-2` for 256 colors. - [`shell`][api-workspace-cli-shell], plugins, and custom workspace builders run through tmuxp itself and need tmuxp 1.74.0. The [compatibility reference][api-workspace-compatibility] records what is implemented and where it differs. ## What it leaves out - **Old tmux.** A tmux below 3.3a, or one that reports a version no release uses, such as `master`, exits 1 with the `tmux_unsupported` code before any command runs. Upgrade tmux and restart the tmux server, or use an earlier CLI release. - **88-color mode.** See `-8` above. - **Starting a server on attach.** The attach that ends a load passes `-N`, so it never starts a server. ## Support and status - **Releases.** Releases are numbered `0.1.N`, and each release increments `N`. The API is not settled: any release may change or remove exported identifiers, and the changelog marks each break. Pin an exact version to avoid one. - **tmux.** 3.3a and newer. - **.NET.** A .NET 8 or .NET 10 runtime. - **Systems.** Linux, including WSL. macOS is best effort, without CI coverage. CI builds on Windows x64. - **Workspace files.** tmuxp's format, in YAML or JSON. - **Python bridge.** It runs the tmux the CLI uses: `LIBTMUX_TMUX` when set, otherwise the `tmux` on `PATH`. ## Documentation - [Command reference](https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/cli/) — every command and option - [Installation walkthrough](https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/guides/installation/) — install, load, and capture on a private socket - [Inspect a loaded session through MCP](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-dotnet/blob/master/src/LibTmux.Mcp/README.md) — let an assistant read your panes - [LibTmux.Workspace](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-dotnet/blob/master/src/LibTmux.Workspace/README.md) — build sessions from C# instead - [Source](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-dotnet/tree/master/src/LibTmux.Workspace.Cli) — the package directory on GitHub - [Changelog](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-dotnet/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) ## License [MIT](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-dotnet/blob/master/LICENSE) [api-workspace-cli]: https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/cli/ [api-workspace-cli-convert]: https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/cli/convert/ [api-workspace-cli-debug-info]: https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/cli/debug-info/ [api-workspace-cli-edit]: https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/cli/edit/ [api-workspace-cli-freeze]: https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/cli/freeze/ [api-workspace-cli-import]: https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/cli/import/ [api-workspace-cli-load]: https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/cli/load/ [api-workspace-cli-ls]: https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/cli/ls/ [api-workspace-cli-search]: https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/cli/search/ [api-workspace-cli-shell]: https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/cli/shell/ [api-workspace-compatibility]: https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/reference/compatibility/ [api-workspace-completion]: https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/cli/completion/ [api-workspace-output]: https://libtmux.org/en/csharp/latest/workspace/reference/output/

go:.github/workflows/tests.yml.content:
name: tests

# A branch with an open pull request would otherwise run this twice per push,
# once for each event, and the two runs compete for the same runners while
# driving real tmux servers. That contention is what makes the timing-sensitive
# tests fail on one of the pair and pass on the other.
#
# A push or pull request runs the oldest and the newest supported tmux. A `v*`
# tag and a dispatch with scope=full run the whole table. scripts/ci-plan.sh
# decides, from .github/ci-matrix.txt, and every tmux lane below takes its
# matrix from that plan.
on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
    tags: ['v*']
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      scope:
        description: edges runs the oldest and newest tmux, full the whole table, custom the tmux-ref list
        type: choice
        options: [edges, full, custom]
        default: edges
      tmux-ref:
        description: With scope=custom, comma-separated tmux versions, tags, branches or commits
        type: string
        default: ''
      go-version:
        description: Comma-separated Go versions; empty runs the normal ones
        type: string
        default: ''
      os:
        description: Runner image for the test and tmux jobs
        type: choice
        options: [ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-22.04]
        default: ubuntu-latest
      tmate:
        description: Open a tmate session on the one tmux lane, which needs a single tmux-ref
        type: choice
        options: ['off', before-tests, on-failure]
        default: 'off'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A superseded push should not keep a matrix this wide running to completion:
# nothing reads the result once a newer commit exists on the same pull request.
# Cancelling is scoped to pull requests so a master push is never interrupted,
# and the SHA in the group key keeps consecutive master pushes in groups of
# their own rather than queued behind one another. A dispatch is a request for
# that run, so its run id keeps one from cancelling or queueing behind another.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.run_id || github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# Every job below names its modules one at a time. `go test ./...` stops at a
# module boundary, so the consumer modules and the benchmarks are invisible to
# the core module's wildcard and would rot unchecked. Go also skips a directory
# whose name begins with an underscore, which is why `examples` is named too.
env:
  # A tmux namespace of this repository's own. Sibling checkouts run their own
  # suites on the same machine, and a shared socket directory is one suite
  # ending servers another is still using.
  TMUX_TMPDIR: /tmp/libtmux-go-ci

jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      tmux: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.tmux }}
      rejected: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.rejected }}
      go-versions: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.go-versions }}
      os: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.os }}
      skip: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.skip }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Inputs reach the script through the environment, never inline.
      - name: Plan the tmux lanes
        id: plan
        env:
          INPUT_SCOPE: ${{ inputs.scope }}
          INPUT_TMUX_REF: ${{ inputs.tmux-ref }}
          INPUT_GO_VERSION: ${{ inputs.go-version }}
          INPUT_OS: ${{ inputs.os }}
          INPUT_TMATE: ${{ inputs.tmate }}
        run: scripts/ci-plan.sh

  # One check to require. A job the plan left out of scope may be skipped; every
  # other job has to have passed. Matrices shrink through the plan, not through
  # an `if` on a matrix leg, so a skipped leg cannot read as a pass.
  required:
    name: required
    if: ${{ always() }}
    needs: [plan, test, generated, api-diff, lint, windows-resolver, fuzz, benchmarks, tmux-matrix, tmux-rejected]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Require every planned job to have passed
        env:
          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
          ALLOW_SKIPPED: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.skip }}
        run: scripts/ci-plan.sh verify

  test:
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 10
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        module: [".", "examples", "workspace", "mcp", "benchmarks", "internal/tools"]
        go-version: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.go-versions) }}
    steps:
      # Whole history, because the gates on staleness compare what is written
      # down against the tags -- the version a source build reports, and the
      # version every go.mod requires -- and a checkout without tags skips them
      # rather than failing. fetch-tags alone does not do it: it drops --no-tags
      # from a depth-1 fetch, and no tag points at the one commit that fetches,
      # so none arrive.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version: ${{ matrix.go-version }}
          cache-dependency-path: ${{ matrix.module }}/go.mod

      - name: Install tmux
        run: ./scripts/apt-get.sh update && ./scripts/apt-get.sh install --yes tmux

      - name: Create the tmux socket directory
        run: mkdir -p "$TMUX_TMPDIR"

      # Coverage names the core module explicitly rather than defaulting to the
      # package under test. The tests that exercise the core live in
      # internal/integration, so counting only the package under test would
      # report the core as uncovered by the tests that cover it.
      #
      # The workspace stays on. GOWORK=off answers whether a module resolves
      # for a stranger, which is a real question answered by the standalone
      # module-metadata test. It cannot also answer whether this tree works,
      # because mcp carries no replace
      # directive and so resolves the core from the proxy. Asking one run both
      # questions is how nineteen commits of core reached the mcp job as a
      # release nobody had built against it.
      - name: Test ${{ matrix.module }}
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.module }}
        env:
          # The floor is only tested if the go command cannot leave it. Left to
          # its default, a go.mod requiring more than the matrix version makes
          # the go command fetch that newer toolchain and pass, so the oldest
          # entry would prove nothing.
          GOTOOLCHAIN: local
        run: |
          tmux -V
          go vet ./...
          "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/test-module.sh" "${{ matrix.module }}" -race -count=1 -coverpkg=./... -coverprofile=coverage.out

      # An artifact name cannot contain a path separator, and one module is
      # nested, so the separator becomes a dash.
      - name: Name the coverage artifact
        id: coverage
        env:
          MODULE: ${{ matrix.module }}
        run: echo "name=coverage-${MODULE//\//-}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ${{ steps.coverage.outputs.name }}
          path: ${{ matrix.module }}/coverage.out
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  # Generated output is checked in, so the check is that regenerating it changes
  # nothing. The Go in the README is generated from the examples, which is what
  # stops a snippet drifting from the program it was copied from.
  generated:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version: stable
          cache-dependency-path: |
            go.mod
            mcp/go.mod

      - name: Regenerate
        run: |
          go generate ./...
          go -C mcp generate ./...

      - name: Report anything regenerating changed
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code; then
            echo "::error::generated files are out of date; run both module generators" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

  # An exported identifier can change or vanish without anything saying so: the
  # changelog is written by hand, and nothing compares what a release exports
  # against what the last one did. This reports that difference into the run
  # summary rather than failing on it, because a `0.1.N` module breaks its API
  # on purpose and a gate that forbids it would be turned off.
  api-diff:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      # Whole history: the comparison needs the tag the last release carries.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version: stable
          cache-dependency-path: |
            go.mod
            workspace/go.mod
            mcp/go.mod

      - name: Report the exported API difference since each module's last tag
        env:
          GORELEASE: golang.org/x/exp/cmd/gorelease@v0.0.0-20250620022241-b7579e27df2b
        run: |
          set -u
          status=0
          for module in . workspace mcp; do
            case $module in
              .) prefix='v' ;;
              *) prefix="$module/v" ;;
            esac
            tag=$(git tag --list "$prefix*" | sort -V | tail -1)
            # A nested module is tagged with its directory, and carries the
            # bare semantic version that tag encodes.
            base=${tag#"$module/"}
            if [ -z "$tag" ]; then
              printf '### %s\n\nNo tag to compare against.\n\n' "$module" \
                >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
              continue
            fi
            printf '### %s since %s\n\n```\n' "$module" "$tag" \
              >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            (cd "$module" && go run "$GORELEASE" -base "$base" 2>&1) \
              >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || status=$?
            printf '```\n\n' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          done
          printf 'gorelease reported status %s; this job does not fail on it.\n' \
            "$status"

  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        module: [".", "examples", "workspace", "mcp", "benchmarks", "internal/tools"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version: '>=1.27.3'
          check-latest: true
          cache-dependency-path: ${{ matrix.module }}/go.mod

      - name: Check formatting
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.module }}
        run: |
          if ! output=$(go run mvdan.cc/gofumpt@v0.12.0 -l .); then
            echo "gofumpt failed" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -n "$output" ]; then
            echo "these files are not gofumpt-formatted:" >&2
            echo "$output" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # verify is off here and run explicitly below. Each module has its own
      # configuration, including module-specific directive policy, so each one
      # must be checked from the directory where lint selects it.
      # The linter must understand the toolchain's compiler export data.
      - uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@v9
        with:
          version: v2.14.0
          working-directory: ${{ matrix.module }}
          verify: false

      # Worth keeping despite the network: golangci-lint run ignores a
      # configuration key it does not recognise and reports no issues, so a
      # misspelled linter setting silently does nothing without this.
      - name: Verify the lint configuration
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.module }}
        run: golangci-lint config verify

      - name: Report known vulnerabilities
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.module }}
        run: go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@v1.6.0 ./...

  # tmux itself does not run on Windows, but constructor-time executable
  # resolution follows Windows PATH, PATHEXT, and current-directory rules.
  # Cross-compilation cannot exercise those filesystem semantics. This is
  # also the only job that compiles workspace/internal/cli's "!unix" files:
  # every other job runs on Linux, where "unix" wins instead.
  windows-resolver:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version: stable
          cache-dependency-path: |
            go.mod
            workspace/go.mod

      - name: Test Windows executable resolution
        run: |
          go vet ./tmux/internal/tmuxcmd
          go test -count=1 -run '^TestResolveExecutable' ./tmux/internal/tmuxcmd

      - name: Vet the workspace module on Windows
        run: go -C workspace vet ./...

  # The fuzz targets already carry regression seeds. A bounded job lets the
  # engine keep searching without turning an open-ended fuzz run into a gate
  # that never completes.
  fuzz:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version: stable
          cache-dependency-path: go.mod

      # go test exits zero with only a warning when -fuzz matches no target.
      # Check the names first so a rename cannot silently disable this job.
      - name: Verify fuzz targets
        run: |
          test "$(go test ./tmux -list '^FuzzDecodeArgsEscapedValueRoundTrip$' | sed -n '1p')" = 'FuzzDecodeArgsEscapedValueRoundTrip'
          test "$(go test ./tmux -list '^FuzzDecodeFormatRecordsRoundTrip$' | sed -n '1p')" = 'FuzzDecodeFormatRecordsRoundTrip'

      - name: Fuzz escaped option values
        run: go test ./tmux -run '^$' -fuzz '^FuzzDecodeArgsEscapedValueRoundTrip$' -fuzztime 30s

      - name: Fuzz format records
        run: go test ./tmux -run '^$' -fuzz '^FuzzDecodeFormatRecordsRoundTrip$' -fuzztime 30s

  # The benchmarks module prints the table BENCHMARKS.md holds. Publishing it
  # here is what lets the checked-in numbers be compared against a run other
  # than the one they were recorded on.
  benchmarks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version: stable
          cache-dependency-path: benchmarks/go.mod

      - name: Install tmux
        run: ./scripts/apt-get.sh update && ./scripts/apt-get.sh install --yes tmux

      - name: Publish the switch matrix
        continue-on-error: true
        working-directory: benchmarks
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$TMUX_TMPDIR"
          {
            echo '### Switch matrix'
            echo
            echo '```'
            go run .
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # The supported tmux range is a claim the README makes, so something has to
  # check it. Ubuntu ships one tmux; version-specific breakage is why this
  # exists -- 3.4 stopped taking split-window's -p that 3.3a and 3.5 both take.
  #
  # This module carries code that only runs on tmux 3.8 and later - JSON
  # layouts, the 3.8 format fields, a popup guard, session-scoped subscriptions
  # - so the table ends with 3.8 and the full scope adds tmux master. Master
  # reports "next-X.Y"; it moves, so its lane is advisory. It runs every
  # module's full suite and is expected to pass: a red master lane means
  # upstream changed something this library has not followed yet, to fix in its
  # own change, and it never blocks the one under review. The only tests that
  # skip on master are the popup tests that need a client overlay, which tmux
  # replaced with a floating pane.
  tmux-matrix:
    name: tmux-matrix (${{ matrix.name }})
    needs: plan
    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.tmux != '[]' }}
    runs-on: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.os }}
    # A tmate session needs longer than a test run does.
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.tmate == 'off' && 10 || 60 }}
    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.advisory }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.tmux) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version: ${{ matrix.go-version }}
          cache-dependency-path: go.mod

      - name: Build tmux ${{ matrix.tmux-version }}
        id: tmux
        uses: ./.github/actions/build-tmux
        with:
          ref: ${{ matrix.tmux-version }}

      # The cache regressions start the lane's own tmux, so a build that the
      # validation would wrongly accept fails here before the module suites run.
      - name: Test the tmux build and cache regressions
        env:
          TMUX_PREFIX: ${{ steps.tmux.outputs.prefix }}
        run: |
          python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/tmux-build-tests"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tmux-build-tests/bin/pip" install --quiet pytest==9.2.0
          export PATH="$TMUX_PREFIX/bin:$PATH"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tmux-build-tests/bin/python" -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider .github/scripts/test_tmux_build.py

      - name: Open a tmate session before the tests
        if: ${{ matrix.tmate == 'before-tests' }}
        uses: mxschmitt/action-tmate@35b54afac29c97fb54faba5b513f8fbd1882f113 # v3.24
        with:
          limit-access-to-actor: true

      - name: Test compatible module coverage against tmux ${{ matrix.tmux-version }}
        env:
          TMUX_PREFIX: ${{ steps.tmux.outputs.prefix }}
          TMUX_EXPECT: ${{ matrix.expect }}
        run: |
          ./scripts/apt-get.sh update
          ./scripts/apt-get.sh install --yes libevent-2.1-7
          export PATH="$TMUX_PREFIX/bin:$PATH"
          actual_version=$(tmux -V)
          # The expected version is a glob: master reports next-X.Y.
          # shellcheck disable=SC2254
          case "$actual_version" in
            $TMUX_EXPECT) ;;
            *) echo "::error::expected $TMUX_EXPECT, got $actual_version" >&2; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          printf '%s\n' "$actual_version"
          mkdir -p "$TMUX_TMPDIR"
          for module in . examples workspace mcp benchmarks internal/tools; do
            echo "--- $module: full suite ---"
            ./scripts/test-module.sh "$module" -count=1
          done

      # These tests skip on every release but the one they exercise, and the
      # step above is not verbose, so a lane that stopped running its own would
      # pass without them. The lane built for the release names them and fails
      # if one does not run and pass. 3.3a is the oldest supported release and
      # runs on every push; the others run with the whole table.
      - name: Run the tests that need exactly tmux ${{ matrix.tmux-version }}
        if: contains(fromJSON('["3.3a", "3.4", "3.5", "3.6", "3.7"]'), matrix.tmux-version)
        env:
          TMUX_VERSION: ${{ matrix.tmux-version }}
          TMUX_PREFIX: ${{ steps.tmux.outputs.prefix }}
        run: |
          export PATH="$TMUX_PREFIX/bin:$PATH"
          test "$(tmux -V)" = "tmux $TMUX_VERSION"
          mkdir -p "$TMUX_TMPDIR"
          set -o pipefail
          case "$TMUX_VERSION" in
            3.3a)
              required='TestRawSelectLayoutIsRefusedWhereItKillsTheServer TestRawRefreshClientClipboardQueryIsRefusedWhereItKillsTheServer'
              ;;
            3.4|3.5|3.6)
              required='TestRawRefreshClientClipboardQueryIsRefusedWhereItKillsTheServer'
              ;;
            3.7)
              required='TestExact37RefusesWindowNamesWithColonOrPeriod TestExact37ConnectionCallRefusesNamesWithColonOrPeriod TestOptionalExact37BreakPaneKeepsItsNamingContract TestOptionalExact37ConnectionCallRefusesRawBreakPane TestOpenControlBindsTheVersionItChecked'
              ;;
          esac
          regex="^($(printf '%s ' $required | sed 's/ $//; s/ /|/g'))\$"
          ./scripts/test-module.sh . -count=1 -v -run "$regex" | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/exact.log"
          for name in $required; do
            grep -q -- "^--- PASS: $name " "$RUNNER_TEMP/exact.log" || { echo "::error::$name did not run and pass"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Tests that put a 3.3a daemon beside this lane's newer client skip
      # without a 3.3a build, and a lane that skips them proves nothing. Lanes
      # with the control client those tests start build 3.3a, name it, and fail
      # if any of the tests does not run and pass.
      - name: Build tmux 3.3a for the older-daemon tests
        id: older
        if: ${{ matrix.control }}
        uses: ./.github/actions/build-tmux
        with:
          ref: '3.3a'

      - name: Run the older-daemon tests against tmux ${{ matrix.tmux-version }}
        if: ${{ matrix.control }}
        env:
          TMUX_PREFIX: ${{ steps.tmux.outputs.prefix }}
          OLDER_PREFIX: ${{ steps.older.outputs.prefix }}
        run: |
          ./scripts/apt-get.sh update
          ./scripts/apt-get.sh install --yes libevent-2.1-7
          export PATH="$TMUX_PREFIX/bin:$PATH"
          export LIBTMUX_OPTIONAL_OLD_TMUX="$OLDER_PREFIX/bin/tmux"
          test "$("$LIBTMUX_OPTIONAL_OLD_TMUX" -V)" = 'tmux 3.3a'
          mkdir -p "$TMUX_TMPDIR"
          set -o pipefail
          run_required() {
            module=$1; shift
            regex="^($(printf '%s|' "$@" | sed 's/|$//'))\$"
            ./scripts/test-module.sh "$module" -count=1 -v -run "$regex" | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/older.log"
            for name in "$@"; do
              grep -q -- "^--- PASS: $name " "$RUNNER_TEMP/older.log" || { echo "::error::$name did not run and pass"; exit 1; }
            done
          }
          run_required . \
            TestOptionalControlRejectsOlderSupportedDaemon \
            TestOptionalColdControlRejectsOlderExecutable \
            TestOptionalColdBootstrapKeepsItsFeatureFloor \
            TestPinnedControlSocketPreventsReplacement \
            TestOptionalRefusalsLeaveOlderCoreStateIntact \
            TestStartControlModeRefusesOlderSupportedDaemon
          run_required workspace TestWorkspaceChoosesAnEligibleTransport
          run_required mcp \
            TestOlderCoreRuntimeKeepsItsProcessLane \
            TestOlderCoreRuntimeBootstrapsWithoutControl \
            TestOlderPasteStagingRefusesBeforeTheFirstChunk \
            TestOlderWaitForTextPollsInsteadOfRefusing

      - name: Open a tmate session after a failure
        if: ${{ failure() && matrix.tmate == 'on-failure' }}
        uses: mxschmitt/action-tmate@35b54afac29c97fb54faba5b513f8fbd1882f113 # v3.24
        with:
          limit-access-to-actor: true

  # The releases below the floor stay in the repository as negative fixtures,
  # and they run with the whole table.
  tmux-rejected:
    needs: plan
    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.rejected != '[]' }}
    runs-on: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 10
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        rejected-version: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.rejected) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version: stable
          cache-dependency-path: go.mod
      - name: Build the supported floor tmux
        id: floor
        uses: ./.github/actions/build-tmux
        with:
          ref: '3.3a'
      - name: Build the rejected tmux ${{ matrix.rejected-version }}
        id: rejected
        uses: ./.github/actions/build-tmux
        with:
          ref: ${{ matrix.rejected-version }}
      # The unpatched 3.3 lane also needs 3.7c, the newer client the
      # stale-executable test starts beside the 3.3a floor build.
      - name: Build the newer client tmux 3.7c
        id: newer
        if: ${{ matrix.rejected-version == '3.3' }}
        uses: ./.github/actions/build-tmux
        with:
          ref: '3.7c'
      - name: Refuse unsupported daemons before effects
        env:
          REJECTED_VERSION: ${{ matrix.rejected-version }}
          FLOOR_PREFIX: ${{ steps.floor.outputs.prefix }}
          REJECTED_PREFIX: ${{ steps.rejected.outputs.prefix }}
          NEWER_PREFIX: ${{ steps.newer.outputs.prefix }}
        run: |
          export PATH="$FLOOR_PREFIX/bin:$PATH"
          export LIBTMUX_REJECTED_TMUX="$REJECTED_PREFIX/bin/tmux"
          export LIBTMUX_FLOOR_TMUX="$FLOOR_PREFIX/bin/tmux"
          test "$(tmux -V)" = 'tmux 3.3a'
          test "$("$LIBTMUX_REJECTED_TMUX" -V)" = "tmux $REJECTED_VERSION"
          mkdir -p "$TMUX_TMPDIR"
          # A skipped test or a filter that matches nothing must fail this job.
          export LIBTMUX_REQUIRE_REJECTED=1
          required='TestCoreMinimumRejectsExplicitOlderDaemon TestCoreMinimumOpaqueExecutableOn33a'
          case "$REJECTED_VERSION" in
            3.0a|3.1c)
              export LIBTMUX_REQUIRE_PRE32=1
              required="$required TestCoreMinimumRefusesDaemonBeforeProbeExisted TestCoreMinimumRefusesExecutableBeforeProbeExisted TestCoreMinimumRefusesPre32DaemonPromptly"
              ;;
          esac
          set -o pipefail
          go test -count=1 -timeout 2m -v ./tmux/internal/integration -run '^TestCoreMinimum' | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/rejected.log"
          for name in $required; do
            grep -q -- "^--- PASS: $name " "$RUNNER_TEMP/rejected.log" || { echo "::error::$name did not run and pass"; exit 1; }
          done
          if [ "$REJECTED_VERSION" = 3.3 ]; then
            # A configured 3.7c executable replaced by the 3.3a floor build must
            # be checked afresh, which needs both on hand.
            name=TestCoreMinimumColdFeatureRequirementUsesFreshExecutable
            PATH="$NEWER_PREFIX/bin:$PATH" go test -count=1 -timeout 2m -v ./tmux/internal/integration -run "^$name\$" | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/cold.log"
            grep -q -- "^--- PASS: $name " "$RUNNER_TEMP/cold.log" || { echo "::error::$name did not run and pass"; exit 1; }
          fi

;;; docs:package
(defpackage #:libtmux.examples
  (:use #:cl)
  (:local-nicknames (#:tm #:libtmux)
                    (#:q #:libtmux.query)
                    (#:j #:libtmux.json)
                    (#:ws #:libtmux.workspace))
  (:export #:inspect-workspace #:create-workspace #:observed-value
           #:apply-workspace-document #:workspace-description
           #:terminate-owned-server #:configuration-report))

(in-package #:libtmux.examples)
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:configuration
(defun configuration-report (client session)
  "Read native configuration text; return an owned report and diagnostic outcomes."
  (let ((outcomes nil))
    (flet ((inspect-text (reader &rest options)
             (multiple-value-bind (text outcome) (apply reader client options)
               (push outcome outcomes)
               text)))
      (let ((report
              (list :options (inspect-text #'tm:show-options-text
                                           :scope :session :target session
                                           :name "status" :include-inherited t)
                    :hooks (inspect-text #'tm:show-hooks-text
                                         :scope :session :target session)
                    :environment (inspect-text #'tm:show-environment-text
                                               :scope :session :target session))))
        (values report (coerce (nreverse outcomes) 'simple-vector))))))
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:inventory
(defun inspect-workspace (socket-path &key (program "tmux"))
  "Acquire one graph from SOCKET-PATH; return owned session/window/pane data."
  (tm:with-client (client :program program :socket-path socket-path)
    (let ((snapshot (tm:fetch-snapshot client)))
      (loop for session across (tm:sessions snapshot)
            collect
            (list :session (tm:name session)
                  :windows
                  (loop for link across (tm:window-links session)
                        for window = (tm:window link)
                        collect (list :index (tm:index link)
                                      :name (tm:name window)
                                      :panes (map 'list #'tm:entity-data
                                                  (tm:panes window)))))))))
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:worker
(defun drive-worker (client session socket-path program worker-path receipt-path)
  "Launch a worker through argv, wait for readiness and verify input consumption.
WORKER-PATH names the shipped worker.sh; RECEIPT-PATH is in the owned demo directory.
Signals operational conditions without retrying a mutation. Calls block."
  (let* ((ready (symbol-name (gensym "example-ready-")))
         (consumed (symbol-name (gensym "example-consumed-")))
         (window (observed-value
                  (tm:new-window client session :name "worker"
                                 :command (list "/bin/sh" worker-path program
                                                socket-path ready consumed receipt-path))))
         (pane (aref (tm:panes window) 0))
         (message "release #{literal}; λ"))
    (tm:run-command client (list "-N" "wait-for" ready)
                    :effect :read :timeout 1 :output-limit 4096)
    (tm:send-text client pane message :enter t)
    (tm:run-command client (list "-N" "wait-for" consumed)
                    :effect :read :timeout 1 :output-limit 4096)
    (let ((receipt (uiop:read-file-string receipt-path :external-format :utf-8)))
      (assert (string= message receipt))
      (list :consumed receipt :pane (tm:id pane)))))
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:condition
(defun cancelled-read (client)
  "Demonstrate typed failure evidence using a read cancelled before acquisition."
  (let ((token (tm:make-cancellation-token)))
    (tm:cancel token)
    (handler-case
        (progn (tm:fetch-snapshot client :cancel-token token)
               (error "A cancelled read unexpectedly completed"))
      (tm:command-cancelled (condition)
        (let ((outcome (tm:error-outcome condition)))
          (list :condition (type-of condition)
                :status (and outcome (tm:outcome-status outcome))
                :phase (and outcome (tm:outcome-phase outcome))))))))
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:outcome
(defun observed-value (outcome)
  "Return an operation's observed value, or signal its observation failure."
  (when (tm:outcome-observation-error outcome)
    (error (tm:outcome-observation-error outcome)))
  (multiple-value-bind (value present-p) (tm:outcome-value outcome)
    (unless present-p
      (error "This operation did not return an observation"))
    value))
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:workspace
(defun create-workspace (client)
  "Extend the demo's WORK session; return a fresh captured graph.
Creates a logs window, a second editor pane, a review session and a shared link.
The caller owns the isolated daemon; repeating this recipe there is an error."
  (let* ((before (tm:fetch-snapshot client))
         (work (find "work" (tm:sessions before) :key #'tm:name :test #'string=)))
    (unless work (error "Start the demo's WORK session first"))
    (let* ((editor-link (aref (tm:window-links work) 0))
           (editor (tm:window editor-link))
           (pane (aref (tm:panes editor) 0))
           (logs (observed-value
                  (tm:new-window client work :name "logs" :command '("/bin/cat"))))
           (review (observed-value
                    (tm:new-session client :name "review" :window-name "notes"
                                          :command '("/bin/cat")))))
      (tm:split-pane client pane :direction :horizontal :command '("/bin/cat"))
      (tm:link-window client editor-link review 7)
      (tm:rename-window client logs "logs #{literal}")
      (tm:fetch-snapshot client))))
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:selection
(defun wide-active-panes (snapshot)
  "Select captured active panes at least 40 cells wide; no tmux commands."
  (loop for pane across (tm:panes snapshot)
        when (and (tm:active-p pane) (>= (tm:width pane) 40))
          collect (tm:entity-data pane)))
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:query
(defparameter *wide-active-filter*
  (q:compile-filter
   :pane
   '(:and (:= :pane/active t)
          (:>= :pane/width 40))))

(defun wide-active-pane-data (snapshot)
  "Return owned data for captured active panes at least 40 cells wide; no I/O."
  (map 'vector #'tm:entity-data
       (q:matching *wide-active-filter* (tm:panes snapshot))))
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:explain
(defun filter-execution (filter)
  "Report that FILTER runs locally and acquires nothing, with the fields it reads."
  (let ((report (q:explain filter)))
    (list :execution (getf report :execution)
          :acquires-p (getf report :acquires-p)
          :fields (getf report :required-fields))))
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:relation
(defparameter *active-session-filter*
  (q:compile-filter
   :session
   '(:any :session/window-links
     (:is :link/window
      (:any :window/panes
       (:= :pane/active t))))))

(defun active-session-data (snapshot)
  "Return owned data for sessions with an active pane; no I/O."
  (map 'vector #'tm:entity-data
       (q:items
        (q:where (q:from (tm:sessions snapshot) :model :session)
                 *active-session-filter*))))
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:regex
(defparameter *cat-command-filter*
  (q:compile-filter
   :pane
   '(:regex-full-match :pane/current-command
     (:cl-ppcre "CAT" :case-insensitive-mode t))))

(defun cat-pane-data (snapshot)
  "Return owned data for captured panes whose command is exactly cat; no I/O."
  (map 'vector #'tm:entity-data
       (q:matching *cat-command-filter* (tm:panes snapshot))))
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:filterdocument
(defun round-trip-filter-document (snapshot)
  "Round-trip the checked regex filter and apply it to one retained snapshot."
  (let* ((document (j:write-filter *cat-command-filter*))
         (restored (j:read-filter document :allow-regex t)))
    (values document
            (map 'vector #'tm:entity-data
                 (q:matching restored (tm:panes snapshot))))))
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:workspacenative
(defun workspace-description ()
  "Build the demo's declaration without I/O. Commands run only during apply.
APP_LABEL seeds the session environment, inherited by subsequent panes."
  (ws:make-workspace
   '(:schema "libtmux.lisp.workspace/1"
     :session
     (:name "declared" :cwd "/tmp"
      :environment #(("APP_LABEL" . "declared"))
      :windows
      #((:name "code" :index 2 :layout :tiled
         :panes #((:shell-command "test \"$APP_LABEL\" = declared && exec /bin/cat")
                  (:command #("/bin/cat"))))
        (:name "shell" :index 5
         :panes #((:command #("/bin/cat")))))))))
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:workspaceconfig
(defun apply-workspace-document (client pathname)
  "Plan and apply one bounded workspace document through explicit CLIENT.
Return the preview steps and application result as two values. Application
shares a 30-second budget; file loading and the preview precede that budget."
  (let* ((workspace (ws:read-workspace pathname))
         (snapshot (tm:fetch-snapshot client))
         (plan (ws:plan-workspace workspace snapshot)))
    (values (ws:plan-steps plan)
            (ws:apply-workspace client workspace :total-timeout 30))))
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:buffers
(defun round-trip-bytes (client)
  "Store and retrieve a named binary buffer, including NUL and invalid UTF-8."
  (let ((bytes (make-array 5 :element-type '(unsigned-byte 8)
                           :initial-contents '(0 10 92 195 255))))
    (tm:set-buffer client bytes :name "example bytes")
    (multiple-value-bind (actual outcome)
        (tm:show-buffer client :name "example bytes")
      (assert (eq :succeeded (tm:outcome-status outcome)))
      (assert (equalp bytes actual))
      actual)))
;;; docs:end

;;; docs:termination
(defun terminate-owned-server (socket-path &key (program "tmux"))
  "Terminate the explicitly selected owned server and return its proven outcome."
  (tm:with-client (client :program program :socket-path socket-path)
    (let ((outcome (tm:kill-server client)))
      (assert (eq :succeeded (tm:outcome-status outcome)))
      (assert (eq :server-terminated (tm:outcome-phase outcome)))
      outcome)))
;;; docs:end

local adapter = require("libtmux.runtime.luv")

local function must(value, err)
    if err ~= nil then
        error(err, 0)
    end
    return value
end

local binary = assert(os.getenv("TMUX_BIN"), "set TMUX_BIN to an absolute tmux executable")
local socket = assert(os.getenv("TMUX_SOCKET"), "set TMUX_SOCKET to an explicit socket")

local result = must(adapter.run(function(runtime)
    local server = must(runtime:connect({ binary = binary, socket_path = socket }):await())

    -- docs:begin main
    local created = must(
        server
            :new_session({ name = "quickstart", window_name = "main", argv = { "/bin/sh" } })
            :await()
    )
    local logs = must(created.session:new_window({ name = "logs", argv = { "/bin/cat" } }):await())
    local split =
        must(logs.pane:split({ direction = "right", percent = 40, argv = { "/bin/cat" } }):await())

    -- The pane signals through the same tmux binary; a bare `tmux` there may be
    -- another build that cannot reach this server.
    local marker = "libtmux-lua-quickstart"
    local signal = ("printf 'libtmux ready\\n'; '%s' wait-for -S %s"):format(binary, marker)
    must(created.pane:send_text(signal):await())
    must(created.pane:send_keys({ "Enter" }):await())
    must(server:command({ "wait-for", marker }, { timeout = 10000 }):await())

    local capture = must(created.pane:capture({ history_lines = 20 }):await())
    assert(must(capture:text()):find("libtmux ready", 1, true), "pane output was not captured")
    print(created.session:reference().id, logs.window:reference().id, split.pane:reference().id)

    must(created.session:kill():await())
    -- docs:end main
    must(server:close():await())
    return true
end))

assert(result)

open Libtmux
module Client = Libtmux_unix.Client
module Workspace = Libtmux_unix.Workspace
module Config = Libtmux_workspace.Config
module Plan = Libtmux_workspace.Plan
module Execution = Libtmux_workspace.Execution

let get = function
  | Ok value -> value
  | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Error.pp error)

let create_window client (initial : Created.t) spawn =
  let created =
    get (Client.create_window client initial.session ~name:"logs" ~spawn)
  in
  let window =
    Snapshot.find_window
      (get (Client.capture client))
      (Window.Target.id created.window)
    |> Option.get
  in
  assert (Window.name window = "logs");
  Printf.printf "created: %s\n" (Window.name window)

let with_demo binary use =
  let channel = Unix.open_process_args_in binary [| binary; "-V" |] in
  let version =
    Fun.protect
      ~finally:(fun () ->
        if Unix.close_process_in channel <> Unix.WEXITED 0 then
          failwith "tmux version discovery failed")
      (fun () -> String.trim (input_line channel))
  in
  if not (String.starts_with ~prefix:"tmux " version) then
    failwith "invalid tmux version";
  let version = String.sub version 5 (String.length version - 5) in
  let spawn =
    Spawn.make
      (Exec
         {
           program = "/bin/sh";
           args = [ "-c"; "echo 'showcase ready'; exec cat -u" ];
         })
  in
  let config =
    match
      Config.make ~directory:(Sys.getcwd ()) ~session:"showcase"
        [ Config.window ~name:"editor" [ Config.pane ~spawn () ] ]
    with
    | Ok value -> value
    | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Config.pp_error error)
  in
  get
    (Libtmux_unix.with_private_daemon ~binary (fun endpoint ->
         let plan =
           match Plan.make ~endpoint ~version ~observed:None config with
           | Ok value -> value
           | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Plan.pp_error error)
         in

"""Outer: compile whole showcase programs against installed packages and run their entry points."""

import contextlib
import ctypes
import json
import os
import selectors
import shutil
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
manifest = json.loads((root / "examples/showcase.json").read_text())
programs = {}
for entry in manifest["examples"]:
    path = (root / entry["file"]).resolve()
    assert path.parent == root / "examples" and path.suffix == ".ml"
    assert entry["whole_file"] and entry["success_exit_code"] == 0
    executable = str(Path(entry["file"]).with_suffix(".exe"))
    assert entry["command"] == [
        "opam",
        "exec",
        "--",
        "dune",
        "exec",
        executable,
        "--",
        "tmux",
    ], "showcase command does not execute its recorded source"
    assert path.stem not in programs, "duplicate showcase program"
    programs[path.stem] = entry
libc = ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True)
if libc.prctl(36, 1, 0, 0, 0):
    raise OSError(ctypes.get_errno(), "PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER")
child_file = Path(f"/proc/self/task/{os.getpid()}/children")


def children():
    return set(map(int, child_file.read_text().split()))


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(
    prefix="libtmux-ocaml-showcase-consumer-"
) as temporary:
    temporary = Path(temporary)
    prefix = temporary / "installed"
    packages = ["libtmux", "libtmux-workspace", "libtmux-unix", "libtmux-eio"]
    subprocess.run(
        [
            "dune",
            "install",
            "--sections=lib,stublibs",
            "--prefix",
            str(prefix),
            *packages,
        ],
        cwd=root,
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
    )
    project = temporary / "consumer"
    project.mkdir()
    runtime_temp = temporary / "runtime-temp"
    runtime_temp.mkdir(mode=0o700)
    (project / "dune-project").write_text("(lang dune 3.24)\n")
    examples = project / "examples"
    examples.mkdir()
    blocking = " ".join(name for name in programs if name != "showcase_watch")
    (examples / "dune").write_text(
        "(executables (names "
        + blocking
        + ") (modules "
        + blocking
        + ") (libraries libtmux libtmux-workspace libtmux-unix unix))\n"
        + "(executable (name showcase_watch) (modules showcase_watch) "
        + "(libraries libtmux libtmux-workspace libtmux-unix libtmux-eio eio_main unix))\n"
    )
    for name in programs:
        source = root / "examples" / f"{name}.ml"
        assert source.is_file(), f"missing standalone showcase: {name}"
        (examples / source.name).write_bytes(source.read_bytes())
    environment = dict(
        os.environ,
        OCAMLPATH=str(prefix / "lib"),
        TMPDIR=str(runtime_temp),
        TMUX="/unrelated/server,99999,0",
        TMUX_PANE="%99999",
    )
    for key in ["DUNE_SOURCEROOT", "DUNE_WORKSPACE"]:
        environment.pop(key, None)
    environment["OPAMSWITCH"] = subprocess.check_output(
        ["opam", "switch", "show", "--safe"], cwd=root, env=environment, text=True
    ).strip()
    resolved = subprocess.check_output(
        ["opam", "exec", "--", "ocamlfind", "query", *packages],
        cwd=project,
        env=environment,
        text=True,
    ).splitlines()
    assert list(map(Path, resolved)) == [
        prefix / "lib" / package for package in packages
    ]
    built = subprocess.run(
        ["dune", "build", "--root", str(project)],
        cwd=project,
        env=environment,
        capture_output=True,
        check=False,
    )
    assert built.returncode == 0, (built.stdout + built.stderr).decode(errors="replace")
    for index, binary in enumerate(sys.argv[1:]):
        actual = str(Path(binary).resolve(strict=True))
        fault = temporary / f"fault-tmux-{index}"
        audit = temporary / f"fault-directory-{index}"
        fault.write_text(
            "#!/usr/bin/env python3\nimport os,subprocess,sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n"
            + "args=sys.argv[1:]\nif '-C' in args and 'new-session' in args:\n"
            + " socket=args[args.index('-S')+1]\n"
            + f" Path({str(audit)!r}).write_text(str(Path(socket).parent))\n"
            + " session=os.environ['LIBTMUX_SHOWCASE_COLLISION']\n"
            + f" subprocess.run([{actual!r},'-S',socket,'new-session','-d','-s',session,'--','/bin/cat','-u'],check=True)\n"
            + f"os.execv({actual!r}, [{actual!r}, *args])\n"
        )
        fault.chmod(0o700)
        cases = [(name, entry, actual, False) for name, entry in programs.items()]
        cases.append(
            (
                "showcase_create_window",
                programs["showcase_create_window"],
                str(fault),
                True,
            )
        )
        cases.append(
            ("showcase_bootstrap", programs["showcase_bootstrap"], str(fault), True)
        )
        for name, entry, program, should_fail in cases:
            previous = children()
            command = [*entry["command"][:-1], program]
            process = subprocess.Popen(
                command,
                cwd=project,
                env=dict(
                    environment,
                    LIBTMUX_SHOWCASE_COLLISION="bootstrap-demo"
                    if name == "showcase_bootstrap"
                    else "showcase",
                ),
                stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            )
            assert process.stdout is not None
            assert process.stderr is not None
            try:
                output, error = process.communicate(timeout=2)
                if should_fail:
                    assert process.returncode == 2 and error, (
                        name,
                        process.returncode,
                        output,
                        error,
                    )
                    assert (
                        entry["expected_stdout_line"].encode()
                        not in output.splitlines()
                    )
                    if name == "showcase_bootstrap":
                        assert (
                            b"workspace " in error and b" did not complete" in error
                        ), error
                        assert (
                            b"new-session" in error and b"no automatic retry" in error
                        ), error
                    directory = Path(audit.read_text())
                else:
                    assert process.returncode == 0 and not error, (
                        name,
                        process.returncode,
                        output,
                        error,
                    )
                    assert (
                        entry["expected_stdout_line"].encode() in output.splitlines()
                    ), (name, "missing expected outcome", output)
                    socket_line = next(
                        line
                        for line in output.splitlines()
                        if line.startswith(b"socket=")
                    )
                    directory = Path(os.fsdecode(socket_line[len(b"socket=") :])).parent
                assert directory.name.startswith("libtmux-ocaml-")
                assert not directory.exists(), "showcase left its private directory"
                for pid in children() - previous:
                    descriptor = os.pidfd_open(pid)
                    try:
                        with selectors.DefaultSelector() as ready:
                            ready.register(descriptor, selectors.EVENT_READ)
                            assert ready.select(1), (
                                f"{name} left owned child {pid} running"
                            )
                        os.waitpid(pid, 0)
                    finally:
                        os.close(descriptor)
                outcome = "startup failure" if should_fail else "installed entry point"
                print(
                    f"PASS {Path(binary).parent.name}: {name}, {outcome} and owned teardown"
                )
            finally:
                if process.poll() is None:
                    process.kill()
                    process.wait(timeout=1)
                while children() - previous:
                    for pid in children() - previous:
                        descriptor = os.pidfd_open(pid)
                        try:
                            with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
                                signal.pidfd_send_signal(descriptor, signal.SIGTERM)
                            with selectors.DefaultSelector() as ready:
                                ready.register(descriptor, selectors.EVENT_READ)
                                assert ready.select(1), (
                                    "owned showcase child did not terminate"
                                )
                            os.waitpid(pid, 0)
                        finally:
                            os.close(descriptor)
                process.stdout.close()
                process.stderr.close()
                for path in runtime_temp.iterdir():
                    if path.is_dir():
                        shutil.rmtree(path)
                    else:
                        path.unlink()

open Libtmux

  | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Error.pp error)

      (Client.create_session client ~name:"linked" ~window_name:"linked-home"
         ~spawn ())
  in
  let pane =
    Snapshot.find_pane
      (get (Client.capture client))
      (Pane.Target.id linked.pane)
    |> Option.get
  in
  let text = "showcase ready" in
  ignore (get (Client.wait_for_text ~timeout:0.5 client pane ~text));
  get
    (Client.link_window client initial.window ~session:linked.session ~index:7);
  get (Client.capture client)
(* docs:end capture-graph *)

module Workspace = Libtmux_unix.Workspace
module Config = Libtmux_workspace.Config
module Plan = Libtmux_workspace.Plan
module Execution = Libtmux_workspace.Execution

let print_graph snapshot =
  Snapshot.sessions snapshot
  |> Iarray.iter (fun session ->
      Session.window_links session
      |> Iarray.iter (fun link ->
          let window = Window_link.window link in
          Printf.printf "%s/%d %s: %d pane(s)\n" (Session.name session)
            (Window_link.index link) (Window.name window)
            (Iarray.length (Window.panes window))));
  assert (Iarray.length (Snapshot.sessions snapshot) = 2);
  assert (Iarray.length (Snapshot.windows snapshot) = 2);
  assert (Iarray.length (Snapshot.window_links snapshot) = 3);
  assert (Iarray.length (Snapshot.panes snapshot) = 2);
  print_endline "graph: 2 sessions, 2 windows, 3 links, 2 panes"

let with_demo binary use =
  let channel = Unix.open_process_args_in binary [| binary; "-V" |] in
  let version =
    Fun.protect
      ~finally:(fun () ->
        if Unix.close_process_in channel <> Unix.WEXITED 0 then
          failwith "tmux version discovery failed")
      (fun () -> String.trim (input_line channel))
  in
  if not (String.starts_with ~prefix:"tmux " version) then
    failwith "invalid tmux version";
  let version = String.sub version 5 (String.length version - 5) in
  let spawn =
    Spawn.make
      (Exec
         {
           program = "/bin/sh";
           args = [ "-c"; "echo 'showcase ready'; exec cat -u" ];
         })
  in
  let config =
    match
      Config.make ~directory:(Sys.getcwd ()) ~session:"showcase"
        [ Config.window ~name:"editor" [ Config.pane ~spawn () ] ]
    with
    | Ok value -> value
    | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Config.pp_error error)
  in
  get
    (Libtmux_unix.with_private_daemon ~binary (fun endpoint ->
         let plan =
           match Plan.make ~endpoint ~version ~observed:None config with
           | Ok value -> value
           | Error error -> failwith (Format.asprintf "%a" Plan.pp_error error)
         in
         let operation = get (Workspace.submit_bootstrap ~binary plan) in
         Fun.protect
           ~finally:(fun () -> get (Workspace.close operation))
           (fun () ->
             let receipt = get (Workspace.await operation) in
             if receipt.status <> Execution.Succeeded then
               failwith "workspace setup failed";
             let client = Option.get (Workspace.client operation) in
             let initial = List.hd (Iarray.get receipt.steps 0).created in
             (match Endpoint.kind endpoint with
             | Endpoint.Socket_path socket ->
                 Printf.printf "socket=%s\n%!" socket
             | Endpoint.Named_socket _ -> ());
             let pane =
               Snapshot.find_pane
                 (get (Client.capture client))
                 (Pane.Target.id initial.pane)
               |> Option.get
             in
             ignore
               (get
                  (Client.wait_for_text ~timeout:0.5 client pane
                     ~text:"showcase ready"));
             use client initial spawn)))

let () =
  let binary = if Array.length Sys.argv = 2 then Sys.argv.(1) else "tmux" in
  let snapshot = with_demo binary capture_graph in
  print_graph snapshot

"""Create a tmux workspace from a workspace :class:`dict`."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
import shutil
import time
import typing as t

from libtmux._internal.query_list import ObjectDoesNotExist
from libtmux.pane import Pane
from libtmux.server import Server
from libtmux.session import Session
from libtmux.window import Window

from tmuxp import exc
from tmuxp.log import TmuxpLoggerAdapter
from tmuxp.util import get_current_pane, run_before_script
from tmuxp.workspace.options import (
    PaneReadiness,
    WorkspaceBuilderOptions,
    resolve_session_shell,
    shell_is_zsh,
)

if t.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from collections.abc import Iterator

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _wait_for_pane_ready(
    pane: Pane,
    timeout: float = 2.0,
    interval: float = 0.05,
) -> bool:
    """Wait for pane shell to draw its prompt.

    Polls the pane's cursor position until it moves from origin (0, 0),
    indicating the shell has finished initializing and drawn its prompt.

    Parameters
    ----------
    pane : :class:`libtmux.Pane`
        pane to wait for
    timeout : float
        maximum seconds to wait before giving up
    interval : float
        seconds between polling attempts

    Returns
    -------
    bool
        True if pane became ready, False on timeout or error

    Examples
    --------
    >>> pane = session.active_window.active_pane

    Wait for the shell to be ready:

    >>> _wait_for_pane_ready(pane, timeout=5.0)
    True
    """
    start = time.monotonic()
    while time.monotonic() - start < timeout:
        try:
            pane.refresh()
        except Exception:
            logger.debug(
                "pane refresh failed during readiness check",
                exc_info=True,
                extra={"tmux_pane": str(pane.pane_id)},
            )
            return False
        if pane.cursor_x != "0" or pane.cursor_y != "0":
            logger.debug(
                "pane ready, cursor moved from origin",
                extra={"tmux_pane": str(pane.pane_id)},
            )
            return True
        time.sleep(interval)
    logger.debug(
        "pane readiness check timed out after %.1f seconds",
        timeout,
        extra={"tmux_pane": str(pane.pane_id)},
    )
    return False
